wins.text: Adjusted EPS of $4.82, up 19% year-over-year; consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY with 60 bps of adjusted margin expansion and 17% adjusted operating income growth
FEC adjusted operating income grew $306M, up 24% YoY, with adjusted operating margin expanding 100 bps — fifth consecutive quarter of YoY margin expansion at FEC
U.S. domestic package revenue grew 12% YoY with average daily domestic volume up 6%, driven by B2B health care wins and new Amazon large/heavyweight shipment business
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $17.80–$19.00 from prior range of $17.20–$19.00, with midpoint implying ~$18.40
Opportunistically repurchased ~$300M of stock in Q2; $1.3B remaining under 2024 buyback authorization; pension cash contribution reduced to $275M from up to $400M

risks.text: MD-11 fleet grounding pressured Q2 adjusted operating income by ~$25M; expected to cause substantially higher costs in Q3 (peak season), with total MD-11 headwind estimated at ~$175M for the year; aircraft not expected to return to service until Q4

FedEx Freight adjusted operating income declined $70M YoY with margin contracting 3 percentage points; full-year Freight EBIT headwind revised from $100M to $300M due to sustained LTL industry weakness and $100M in spin-related separation costs

~$1B headwind to adjusted operating profit from global trade policy changes, including ~25% reduction in trans-Pacific Asia outbound capacity and ~35% reduction in third-party capacity; international export ADV expected to remain pressured in H2
~$600M year-over-year headwind to adjusted operating income in H2 from three discrete items: variable incentive compensation accruals (~$265M), LTL softness (~$160M), and MD-11 grounding (~$175M)
Expiration of USPS contract created a $30M headwind in Q2; higher wage and purchased transportation rates partially offset FEC operating income gains

guidance_items.detail: FY26 adjusted EPS raised to $17.80–$19.00 from prior $17.20–$19.00; midpoint of $18.40 implies Q3 sequentially lower than Q2, Q4 to be strongest quarter of the year

Consolidated FY26 revenue growth now expected at 5%–6%; FEC midpoint implies ~7% YoY revenue growth; FedEx Freight now expected approximately flat to slightly down vs. prior expectation of modest growth
FEC adjusted operating margin expected up slightly at midpoint for FY26; Freight margin expected down YoY
FedEx Freight FY26 revenue revised to approximately flat to slightly down YoY; adjusted operating income headwind revised from $100M to $300M
FY26 CapEx target maintained at $4.5B; YTD CapEx of $1.4B

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Competitive risk from UPS potentially regaining USPS relationship and Teamsters contract advantages pressuring FedEx domestic volume share in FY27
Potential tariff policy reversal (Supreme Court ruling) as a tailwind to international trade volumes and the $1B headwind estimate
Network 2.0 margin flow-through timing — analysts questioned why 24% volume integration wasn't producing more visible financial margin impact yet
